name: Jimmy Dorsey
description: '''James Francis Dorsey''' (February 29, 1904 – June 12, 1957) was an American [[jazz]] [[Clarinet|clarinetist]], [[Saxophone|saxophonist]], composer, and [[big band]] leader. He recorded and composed the jazz and pop standards "[[I'm Glad There Is You]] (In This World of Ordinary People)" and "[[It's the Dreamer in Me]]". His other major recordings were "[[Tailspin (song)|Tailspin]]", "[[John Silver (song)|John Silver]]", "[[So Many Times]]", "[[Amapola (song)|Amapola]]", "Brazil" ("[[Aquarela do Brasil]]"), "[[Pennies from Heaven (song)|Pennies from Heaven]]" (with [[Bing Crosby]], [[Louis Armstrong]], and [[Frances Langford]]), "Grand Central Getaway", and "[[So Rare]]". He played clarinet on the seminal jazz standards "[[Singin' the Blues (Sam M. Lewis, Joe Young, Con Conrad and J. R. Robinson song)|Singin' the Blues]]" in 1927 and the original 1930 recording of "[[Georgia on My Mind]]", which were inducted into the [[Grammy Hall of Fame]].
